subject: Request: availability cushion & scaled monthly credit model for Hedron Health Dedicated
messages:
From: Lauren Park <lauren.park@hedronhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Evan Cho <evan.cho@hedronhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Availability cushion request for Dedicated cluster (Hedron PHI workloads)

Hi Marissa —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We ran a brief readiness review with our infra and compliance teams and there is one sticking point on the SLA we need to resolve before procurement can proceed.

Our PHI workloads will be hosted on the dedicated pool you proposed, but our security team requires a documented exception for the standard 99.99% uptime obligation when we enter quarterly bulk-maintenance windows. Operationally, we need a 30-minute per-month availability cushion (i.e., agreed carveout) for planned cluster-wide reboots and patching.

Concretely, the ask is: 1) allow a planned-maintenance carveout of up to 30 minutes per month that does not count against monthly uptime, and 2) if unplanned downtime occurs, adopt a graduated credit model that scales linearly per minute beyond the cushion rather than a single monthly credit threshold.

I attached a short doc and an example spreadsheet of how we model credits. Can Redwood confirm if this is an acceptable exception to the public SLA template and, if so, propose language we can circulate to legal? We prefer to keep the overall availability commitment close to 99.99% but need the mechanics spelled out.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — our procurement window closes end of next week.

—Lauren
Lauren Park
Sr. Director, IT Procurement
Hedron Health

Attachment(s): Hedron_Custom_SLA_Diff_v1.docx (docx, 42 KB), service-credit-scale-proposal.xlsx (xlsx, 18 KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Park <lauren.park@hedronhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2026 12:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Availability cushion request for Dedicated cluster (Hedron PHI workloads)

Hi Lauren —

Thanks for the clear note and the attachments — very helpful context. Short answer: yes, we can support a documented planned-maintenance carveout and a per-minute graduated credit band for unplanned downtime, but we need to agree the operational definitions and the guardrails so the construct is predictable for both sides.

A few immediate clarifications from our side:
- "Planned-maintenance carveout": we typically define planned maintenance as events scheduled >= 72 hours in advance and published to the customer-facing maintenance calendar. We can allocate a 30-minute per-month carveout for cluster-wide reboots in the Dedicated plan, provided maintenance windows are scheduled and limited to the pre-agreed calendar.
- "Graduated credit model": Redwood's standard crediting uses monthly uptime bands. To support per-minute scaling we'll propose a linear minutes-to-credit function (example below) with a monthly cap to bound exposure.
- "SLA arithmetic: with a 30-minute monthly carveout, our effective uptime commitment will be described both as a gross % (99.99%) and a net operational commitment that references the carveout mechanics.

Attached is an initial redline to your doc and an example credit scale we believe is balanced. Can Karthik review the technical ops definitions (maintenance scheduling, notification, pre/post-checklist) and Marcus scope any monthly-cap / insurance-style guardrails?

We can turn this around as a formal addendum for legal if you're ok with the approach.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachment(s): Redwood_redline_Hedron_SLA.docx (docx, 35 KB), credit-scale-proposal.csv (csv, 6 KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Lauren Park <lauren.park@hedronhealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2026 08:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Availability cushion request for Dedicated cluster (Hedron PHI workloads)

Lauren —

Thanks — quick operational notes from the infra perspective:

1) Maintenance definition: agreed — >=72h notice and publish to the maintenance calendar. For cluster-wide reboots we will batch low-traffic zones and target a single 30-minute window per month.

2) Detection and measurement: Redwood measures downtime from successful inference request latencies exceeding the availability threshold OR inability to receive TCP connections to the serving tier. We'll include our measurement doc as an exhibit so there's no ambiguity on how minutes are counted.

3) Credit scaling proposal (high level):
   - 0–30 minutes / month (planned carveout): 0 credits.
   - 31–180 minutes: incremental credit = (minutes_over_cushion / 60) * (monthly_service_fee / 720) — effectively pro-rated hours with a multiplier to reflect severity.
   - >180 minutes: capped at 30% of monthly fee unless otherwise negotiated for catastrophic SLA breach.

4) Monthly cap: propose a 30% cap on total credits for the month. This protects both parties and keeps worst-case exposure bounded. If Hedron needs a higher cap we can discuss an insurance or premium SLA tier.

I'll attach the measurement exhibit and a short draft addendum to the SLA language we can insert into section 2 (Availability & Credits). If this looks ok I can hand to Marcus to translate into legal-friendly phrasing for the amendment.

Karthik
VP, Dedicated Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachment(s): measurement-exhibit.txt (txt, 9 KB), ops-addendum-draft.txt (txt, 4 KB)

From: Lauren Park <lauren.park@hedronhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Evan Cho <evan.cho@hedronhealth.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 16:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Availability cushion request for Dedicated cluster (Hedron PHI workloads)

Marissa / Karthik —

Appreciate the rapid turn. The team reviewed the proposed mechanics and the per-minute credit scale is reasonable. A couple of follow-ups before we route to legal:

1) Measurement exhibit: please add a short clause that during any contested incident both sides will exchange raw metrics (request logs, start/end timestamps) and engage the Redwood on-call within 1 hour. Hedron's compliance lead wants an audit trail for minutes counted.

2) Monthly cap: Hedron accepts the 30% cap but asks for an escalation path if a sequence of repeated months exceeds 20% in two consecutive quarters (automated review + joint runbook).

3) Draft language: can Marcus drop the addendum into the same doc and highlight the specific replacement paragraphs for the Availability section so our legal team sees the delta cleanly?

If you can send the edited exhibit/addendum by Friday we'll start legal review.

Thanks —

—Lauren
Sr. Director, IT Procurement
Hedron Health
